title: Praying Alone in the Dark
script: Narrator: [tired] Last night, I woke up alone at three in the morning, and the whole house was completely silent.
Narrator: [sleepily] My body felt heavy, and part of me wanted to simply close my eyes and sleep again.
Narrator: But I remembered something my grandmother always told me when I was still a young girl.
Narrator: [remembering] She said, the sweetest prayers happen quietly, when nobody else is even awake to witness them.
Narrator: [determined] So I got up slowly, washed my face with cold water, and prayed quietly in the dark room.
Narrator: [calmly] No one saw me. No one knew. It was just me, the darkness, and one small, honest moment.
Narrator: I used a small light and kept the room quiet. The important part was my intention, not the darkness.
Narrator: [focused] Somewhere in the middle of that prayer, I stopped thinking about being tired, and I simply felt present.
Narrator: I have prayed in front of others many times, at the mosque, at family gatherings, in crowded rooms.
Narrator: Those prayers matter too. This private prayer simply helped me focus in a different way.
Narrator: [peacefully] Afterward, I felt a strange, gentle peace that stayed with me for the rest of the morning.
Narrator: Nobody complimented me for waking up. Nobody even knew it happened, and that was exactly the point.
Narrator: [reflective] I learned that private devotion can train my sincerity because no person is there to praise me.
Narrator: Now, some nights, I set an early alarm on purpose, just to sit quietly with Allah while the world sleeps.
Narrator: [sincerely] Nobody applauds these quiet nights. No one ever will. And somehow, that has become exactly why I love them.

quiz.question: What time did the narrator wake up?
quiz.explanation: The narrator says she woke up alone at three in the morning.

quiz.question: What did the narrator's grandmother say about prayer?
options: Sleep is more important than prayer
The sweetest prayers happen quietly, when nobody else is awake to witness them
Prayer should always be shown to others
Mornings are the only good time to pray
quiz.explanation: Her grandmother said the sweetest prayers happen quietly, when nobody else is awake to witness them.

quiz.question: Why did the narrator not turn on the light?
options: She did not want the moment to feel prepared or performed
She could not find the switch
quiz.explanation: She says she did not turn on a light because she did not want it to feel prepared or performed.

quiz.question: How did this private prayer feel compared to praying in front of others?
quiz.explanation: She says this prayer felt different from praying with others, more hers somehow.

quiz.question: What does the narrator now sometimes do on purpose?
options: Set an early alarm to sit quietly with Allah while the world sleeps
quiz.explanation: She now sets an early alarm on purpose to sit quietly with Allah while the world sleeps.

quiz.question: What time did the narrator wake?
quiz.explanation: The whole house was quiet at that early hour.

quiz.question: What did the grandmother teach?
options: Quiet prayer can be sweet and sincere
quiz.explanation: Her advice encouraged worship without an audience.

quiz.question: What did the narrator do before praying?
quiz.explanation: The narrator moved past tiredness and prepared to pray.

quiz.question: What helped the narrator focus?
quiz.explanation: No one else was present to watch or praise.

quiz.question: What matters more than praying in darkness?
quiz.explanation: The revised script directly separates sincerity from lighting.
